writing.overall_comment: A well-scoped, boundary-conscious iOS subagent whose main weaknesses are a slightly thin description and notable redundancy between its principles, best-practices, and checklist sections.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description clearly names the domain (Swift 6/SwiftUI iOS apps) so routing is easy, but it omits trigger cues like when *not* to use it or task types (feature build vs. debugging) that would sharpen main-agent routing.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, stack, workflow, and quality checklist are explicit and opinionated, but there is no stated output contract (e.g., what to return to the caller, how to report verification results).

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: A dedicated Boundaries section cleanly excludes non-iOS work, project-level build/signing/CI changes, and system architecture, and specifies hand-back triggers for ambiguous requirements.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The body repeats the same concurrency/separation-of-concerns guidance across Core Principles, Best Practices, Workflow, and Quality Checklist, so the token budget could be trimmed without losing substance.

suggestions: In the Core Principles section, keep the primary concurrency/separation-of-concerns guidance and replace its repeated explanations in Best Practices, Workflow, and Quality Checklist with brief cross-references.
Trim the Best Practices and Workflow sections so each concurrency/separation-of-concerns point adds new actionable detail instead of restating the same rule.
Condense the Quality Checklist by merging duplicate concurrency/separation-of-concerns items into a single item to reduce tokens while preserving the guidance.
